title: Custom-designed Laser-based Heating Apparatus for Triggered Release of Cisplatin from Thermosensitive Liposomes with Magnetic Resonance Image Guidance
protocol: Dissolve DPPC, MSPC, and mPEG2000-DSPE lipids in chloroform.
Heat the vial containing the dissolved lipids at 60°C for 30 seconds.
Remove chloroform using a rotary evaporator.
Place lipid film under high-pressure vacuum overnight.
Hydrate the lipid film with 5 ml of 0.1N Tris buffer (pH 7.4) for 1 hour.
Weigh DPPG and CDDP powder, then hydrate with 5 ml of 0.1N Tris buffer containing 30% ethanol (pH 7.4) for 1 hour while stirring at 70°C.

For Gd-HTLC formulation, weigh the same amount of DPPG lipid and CDDP powder, then hydrate with a mixture of 2.5 ml of Gd-HP-DO3A solution and 2.5 ml of 0.1N Tris buffer containing 30% ethanol (pH 7.4) for 1 hour while stirring at 70°C.
Combine the lipid mixture and the lipid drug mixture, then hydrate for 1 hour.
Vortex every 15-20 minutes during hydration process.
Assemble the 10-ml extruder with two stacks of 200 nm polycarbonate filters.
Connect the thermobarrel of the extruder to a circulating water bath at 70 °C.
Connect the extruder to a compressed nitrogen tank.
Transfer the mixture into the extruder chamber immediately after hydration.
Open the nitrogen flow (set pressure to 200 psi) to extrude liposomes through membranes.
Collect liposomes in a 50 ml tube.
Keep the tube in a hot water bath (70 °C) at all times during extrusion.
Repeat the process of extruding liposomes five times.
Disassemble the extruder and change to two stacks of 100 nm polycarbonate filters.
Reassemble the extruder and set pressure to 400 psi.
Extrude liposomes ten times through the new filter setup.
Collect sample from final extrusion into a 15 ml tube.
Cool down liposomes to room temperature (RT).
Centrifuge at 1,000 x g for 3 min to precipitate insoluble CDDP.
Dialyze liposomes overnight against 0.9% saline in dialysis tubing with a 15,000 molecular weight cutoff under sterile conditions.
Dilute 10 µl of liposomes in 990 µl distilled water.
Measure the size distribution of HTLC and Gd-HTLC using dynamic light scattering.
Perform three measurements with ten runs each.
Dilute 40 µl of liposomes in 3960 µl distilled water.
Prepare standard solutions of platinum and gadolinium ranging from 0.1 to 20 µg/ml.
Measure platinum and gadolinium concentrations using ICP-AES at three different wavelengths.
Perform three measurements at each wavelength for an average result.
Determine the gel to liquid crystalline phase transition temperature (Tm) of HTLC liposome formulation using DSC.
Load 5-10 mg of HTLC into a DSC pan and use an empty pan as reference.
Use a scan rate of 5 °C/min from 0 °C to 60 °C for DSC analysis.
Wrap liposomes in aluminum foil to prevent light exposure.
Store wrapped liposomes at 4 °C.
Incubate 50 g gel filtration beads in 400 ml 0.9% saline at room temperature for 3-4 hours.
Roll up a piece of glass wool, wet with 0.9% saline and place it into the tip of a 1 ml syringe.
Press glass wool to fill approximately 0.05-0.1 ml of the syringe.
Gradually add about 1 ml gel filtration media into the syringe using a glass pipette.
Place the syringe into a 15 ml tube and centrifuge at 1,000 x g for 3 minutes.
Remove spin column from centrifuge and place it into a 15 ml tube.
Sample 400 μl of HTLC or Gd-HTLC into 8 1-dram glass vials.
Incubate the vials in a temperature controlled water bath at either 37 °C or 42 °C.
Remove one vial at each time point (5, 15, 30 and 60 min) and place it on ice immediately after removal.
Add 100 μl of 0.9% saline into the prepared spin column.
Add 100 μl of HTLC or Gd-HTLC before incubation (control) or after incubation in the water bath into the spin column.
Centrifuge at 1,000 x g for 3 min.
Remove the syringe from the tube and dilute the solution in the tube for ICP-AES analysis.
Place the animal in a clean cage without the company of other animals after surgery.
Monitor until sufficient consciousness is regained.
Culture ME-180 cells in α-MEM supplemented with 10% FBS and antibiotics.
Harvest the cells and keep them in complete media before inoculation.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Inoculate each donor mouse to bear an intramuscular (i.m.) ME-180 tumor.
Purchase female SCID mice aged 6-8 weeks, approximately 20 g from an in-house breeding facility.
Anesthetize a female SCID mouse.
Inject 1 x 10^6 ME-180 cells into the gastrocnemius muscle of the hind limb using a 27 G needle.
Measure tumor size using a caliper until tumors have reached 9-12 mm in their longest dimension.
Terminate the study if the tumor exceeds 12 mm or compromises normal behavior, ambulation, food and water intake.
Implant tumor pieces from donor mice into recipient mice.
Anesthetize a donor mouse using 5% isofluorane.
Euthanize the mouse using cervical dislocation under anesthesia.
Remove the donor tumor from the donor mouse.
Cut the tumor into cubic fragments of 2-3 mm³.
Anesthetize a recipient mouse using 5% isofluorane.
Inject 100 μl of 0.5 mg/ml meloxicam subcutaneously before surgery.
Apply iodine surgical scrub solution, then 70% ethanol, and lastly iodine solution to the shaved skin.
Shave the left hind limb of the recipient mouse.
Make an incision at the level of skin.
Insert one donor tumor piece subcutaneously through the incision.
Close the incision using 1-2 wound clip(s).
Remove the clips 3-5 days after implantation.
Cut two small holes, each 5 mm in diameter, between the outer chambers and the larger middle chamber.
Pass a 400 µm cut-end fiber connected to the laser into one of the outer chambers through a 600 µm diameter hole.
Deliver light from the laser into the outer chambers using the connected fiber.
Calibrate the illuminator light delivery with respect to the laser power setting using a NIST calibrated 50 mm integrating sphere.
Calculate the light distribution in the tumor using Monte Carlo simulations based on a simplified geometry of the tumor.
Generate the Monte Carlo code in a custom algorithm written with a commercial computational software package.
Model the tumor as a hemisphere lying on a flat skin line with a diameter matching the average tumor dimension of 7 mm at the skin surface and a height of 5 mm.
Model homogeneous illumination of the surface by randomly launching photons throughout the exposed hemisphere and direct at the center of the sphere.
Use optical properties including absorption, µa = 0.025 mm-1.
Include scattering, µs = 10 mm-1.
Specify anisotropy factor, g = 0.9.
Set refractive index, n=1.4.
Perform measurements using one million photons in the calculation.
Calibrate setup before any in vivo heating experiments.
Connect one end of a laser fiber to the laser device.
Attach the other end of the laser fiber to the illuminator.
Anesthetize the animal with 5% isofluorane.
Insert a 27 G injection catheter into the lateral tail vein of the mouse.
Place a 22 G catheter into the center of the tumor.
Insert a fiber optic temperature probe into the hollow catheter for monitoring.
Cover the entire tumor with the illuminator.
Set initial laser power to 0.8-1 W.
Turn on the laser and wait for the temperature to rise.
Adjust laser power between 0.1-0.8 W to maintain tumor temperature at 42 °C.
Measure the temperature distribution of the heated tumor using MRT with PRF-shift method.
Conduct measurements in conjunction with fiber optic temperature probe readings.

Acquire thermometry images at 10 sec intervals using a 2D-FLASH pulse sequence (echo time 4.5 msec; repetition time 156.25 msec) with 312 x 312 µm in-plane resolution and 2 mm slice thickness in a single slice at the level of the fiber optic temperature probe.
Perform T1-weighted imaging prior to and 20 min after administration of Gd-HTLC.
Preheat the tumor on the left hind limb for 5 min at 42 °C prior to injection of Gd-HTLC.
Heat the tumor for an additional 20 min post-injection.
Inject Gd-HTLC during heating treatment at a dose of 66.3 mg/kg Gd-HP-DO3A and 1.4 mg/kg CDDP.
Use the tumor on the right hind limb as an unheated control.

Acquire dynamic MR images (36 x 20 mm field-of-view, 200 x 200 µm in-plane resolution, 2 mm slice thickness) to monitor Gd-HP-DO3A release at 12 sec intervals for the entire 20 min post administration of Gd-HTLC.
Begin MR imaging acquisition 30 sec prior to injection.
